text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Otology (neurotology) consultation in two weeks, with audiometry, to confirm the cause of the attacks and plan treatment
  • Diagnostic work-up at intake: ear and neurological examination, positional testing, blood count, kidney function and electrolytes, calcium, uric acid, TSH and urinalysis; a symptom diary of each attack (start, duration, hearing, tinnitus, ear fullness, headache, light sensitivity); formal audiometry at the otology visit
  • Meclizine only for severe attacks, for no more than three days at a time; sit or lie down at the first warning; no driving, ladders or swimming alone while attacks are active
  • Depression: PHQ-9 at every visit, a structured diagnostic interview at the next visit, and a safety plan with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number
  • Stone history: drink enough water to pass at least 2.5 liters of urine a day; serum calcium and uric acid at intake; stone analysis and metabolic testing if another stone occurs
  • Ménière disease: education; sodium 1,500 to 2,300 mg a day; caffeine and alcohol limited; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily as maintenance, with sodium and potassium checked at the next visit; no betahistine; MRI of the internal auditory canals with gadolinium; repeat audiogram at about three months; intratympanic steroid held in reserve if disabling attacks continue after three months
  • Recurrent depression: weekly cognitive behavioral therapy with behavioral activation, and sertraline 25 mg daily for a week, then 50 mg, by shared decision; sodium checked on sertraline with the thiazide
  • Right ureteral stone: naproxen for pain, tamsulosin as medical expulsive therapy for up to four weeks, urine strained and the stone sent for analysis, and renal ultrasound after passage
  • Vestibular rehabilitation for unsteadiness between attacks: a home program taught by a vestibular physical therapist
  • Stone prevention from the 24-hour urine: fluids to at least 2.5 liters of urine a day, sodium restriction with a dietitian, normal dietary calcium, citrus fruit for citrate, thiazide continued, and a repeat 24-hour urine in about six months

resource.description: Recognizing and managing Ménière disease in a 43-year-old man with attacks of spinning vertigo, roaring tinnitus and muffled hearing in one ear, under the AAO-HNS 1521 clinical practice guideline and the Bárány Society criteria: a careful history of attack duration and ear symptoms, audiometry to document low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, MRI to exclude a vestibular schwannoma, vestibular migraine and stroke in the differential, salt and caffeine advice, a diuretic as maintenance, the weak evidence for betahistine, limited use of vestibular suppressants, vestibular rehabilitation for chronic imbalance, and intratympanic steroids held in reserve; recurrent depression recognized alongside a frightening chronic illness, with a DSM-5-TR diagnosis, the PHQ-9, a structured safety assessment, CBT and an SSRI by shared decision under the APA 1520 guideline, and the sodium risk of an SSRI with a thiazide; an acute ureteral stone in a man with an earlier stone, with medical expulsive therapy, stone analysis and a 24-hour urine to guide prevention under the AUA guidelines; and preventive care at 43.
